newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-NOAH'S FRANCE TO MEET DUTCH IN FED CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOAH'S FRANCE TO MEET DUTCH IN FED CUP FINAL.

text.p: Successful Davis Cup coach Yannick Noah carried his winning formula into women's tennis on Sunday, guiding France to their first Fed Cup final where they will meet the Netherlands.
With their semifinal against Belgium level at 2-2 in Nice, France's Nathalie Tauziat and Alexandra Fusai clinched the tie with a 3-6 6-2 7-5 doubles win over Els Callens and Laurence Courtois.

In Prague, Dutch doubles pair Miriam Oremans and Manon Bollegraf beat Jana Novotna and Eva Martincova of the Czech Republic to secure their country's place in the final to be held in the Netherlands on October 4 and 5.
France had taken part in seven Fed Cup semifinals but had never made it to the final.
Noah was approached to lead France's Fed Cup campaign after leading the country's men's team to Davis Cup titles in 1991 and last year.
"I'm ever so happy to be in the final. I've already lived the same emotion with the boys and it's unforgettable," Noah said.
"It'll be fantastic with the girls too. It's to experience moments like this that I've accepted to captain them. But I didn't expect us to go this far in my first season with them."
The Dutch pair won 6-4 7-6 in failing light after a nail-biting semifinal on the clay of Prague's Stvanice Stadium.

Oremans, who had already beaten Adriana Gresi in a dramatic three-set match to keep the Dutch level at 2-2, led her team's jubilant orange-clad supporters in a dance around the court after their victory.
World number two Novotna had earlier beaten Brenda Schultz-McCarthy, ranked 14, in straight sets.

The Czechs had appeared to be on their way to victory when Gresi saved three match points at 4-5 in the third set. However, clearly in distress with severe cramp, she went on to squander her own match points and lost the third set 9-7.
Gresi replaced Sandra Kleinova, who played singles on Saturday but was forced to withdraw through illness.
Gresi had to leave the court for several minutes while Czech coach Hana Mandlikova and other team staff massaged her aching legs.
France's victory was all the more spectacular as they were without injured Mary Pierce, who pulled out because of a sore right arm.
Noah also took risks ahead of the tie played at the French Riviera resort of Nice, picking Fusai rather than veteran Tauziat to play the singles.
But the gamble paid off against the Belgians, who beat favourites Spain in the previous round, as Fusai is more of a claycourt specialist than Tauziat.
Fusai beat Belgian number one Sabine Appelmans, but lost to Dominique van Roost in the singles. Sandrine Testud also beat Appelmans and fell to van Roost.
